question: Is a 1-D |omega| refine viable — is truth-|omega| the unique global minimum over the full LS-bracket (no aliasing), and does a findable min survive realistic anchor-quality q error?
hypothesis: Truth-|omega| is the unique global min over the full bracket (1-D scan has nothing to fall into) and the refine recovers correct |omega| even under several degrees of q error, moving the binding constraint to anchor q-accuracy.
narrative_md: The 1-D |omega|-refine is viable: over the full LS-bracket (8.6-142x wide) with q+dir at truth, truth-|omega| is the unique global minimum — 1 local min below rho=8, zero aliases on all three seeds. The refine recovers correct |omega| even at 15 deg q error (<=3% slow, <=0.4% fast). But q-error sets a regime-dependent fit floor: the fast seed needs q within ~1-3 deg even with perfect |omega|, tighter than the 5-15 deg LM grab radius. |omega| is solved as a separable axis; the binding constraint moves to anchor q-accuracy. Holds q/dir at truth and perturbs truth-q -> oracle_clean false.
